_readme: AECI-647 / PH-6 — docs/POSTHOG_MIGRATION_SPEC.md §AW6.
Every dashboard and insight in the AECi PostHog observability plane, as data. apply.sh
is a thin applier over this file; it invents nothing.
Shapes verified live against project 354071 on 2026-08-24: dashboard-create,
insight-create (DataVisualizationNode + HogQLQuery), and every query below compiled and
executed. They return ZERO ROWS today because the AECI-642 transport has not shipped —
that is expected, not a defect. See README.md §"What is verified and what is not".
Two shape rules, both load-bearing:
- Board insights may return any number of rows.
- ALERT-SOURCE insights (dashboard "AECi — What the alerts are watching") MUST be an
aggregate with NO GROUP BY, so they always return exactly one row. A query that can
return zero rows gives its alert nothing to evaluate.
Field guide:
name          Pushed to PostHog. Written for whoever is READING the board, in plain
English, with no issue ids, spec refs or metric names in it.
description   Pushed to PostHog. One to three sentences: what the tile shows, and any
caveat that changes how you read the number. Same plain-English rule.
notes         NOT pushed. Engineering provenance — Datadog lineage, the reason a
query is shaped the way it is, the accepted narrowings. This is where
everything that used to sit in `description` now lives; it is kept
verbatim so nothing was lost when the descriptions were humanised.
previousNames NOT pushed as a field, but READ by apply.sh: if an object with `name`
is absent, it looks these up in order and RENAMES the match in place.
Without it a rename creates a duplicate and orphans the original,
because PostHog objects are matched by exact name. Append, never edit:
the chain has to reach back to whatever is live on the oldest project.

dashboards.name: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
previousNames: AECi — Traffic (SSR + API)
dashboards.description: How much work the site is doing and how well it is going: how many pages and API calls we served, how fast they came back, and what share of them failed. Counts only requests our own servers handled — a page served straight from Cloudflare's edge cache never reaches us, so this is not a visitor count.
dashboards.notes: Ported from observability/datadog/dashboard.json (Phase 2, AECI-66). Worker-side request volume, latency and error rate for both Workers. NOTE (WC-8 / AECI-322): under native Workers Cache a HIT skips the SSR Worker entirely, so cache_status is MISS / non_cacheable only — there is no hit series, and these are MISS / Worker-run volume. Edge HIT rate lives on the Cloudflare Workers dashboard.

dashboards.name: AECi — Search
previousNames: AECi — Search (Algolia + browser)
dashboards.description: Whether search works end to end: the job that copies our catalogue into Algolia, whether the two copies have drifted apart, and how fast and how reliably searches run in visitors' browsers. The browser numbers cover only visitors who accepted analytics cookies, so treat them as a sample rather than a total.
dashboards.notes: Ported from observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json (Phase 3, AECI-141/140/174/266). Algolia sync health, index drift, the orphan sweep, and browser search telemetry. The two browser widgets were sourced from the retiring Datadog RUM aeci.search.query action and now read the consent-gated search_performed event instead (spec §3.9) — a deliberate narrowing from all searches to the consented slice.

dashboards.name: AECi — Home page numbers and page-view logging
previousNames: AECi — Home / Stats
dashboards.description: The two things behind the home page that can break without anyone noticing: the daily job that works out the headline counts shown on the home page, and the background write that records every page view. Neither shows a visitor an error when it fails, so this board is how you find out.
dashboards.notes: Ported from observability/datadog/dashboard-home-stats.json (Phase 4, AECI-180). The two silent-failure surfaces behind the home page: the daily home-stats compute cron and the deferred page_views write.

dashboards.name: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
previousNames: AECi — Auth / Reviews / Moderation
dashboards.description: The signed-in side of the site: people signing in, reviews being submitted, the automatic screen that scores reviews for abusive language, and how big and how old the moderation queue has grown.
dashboards.notes: Ported from observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json (Phase 5, AECI-206). Sign-ins (emitted by the SSR Worker at /auth/callback, so service=aeci-web not aeci-api), review submits, moderation actions, toxicity scoring, and the daily moderation-queue gauges.

dashboards.name: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
previousNames: AECi — Requests / Linear pipeline
dashboards.description: When someone submits a claim or a correction on the site we open a Linear issue for it and keep the two in step. This board shows whether that hand-off is working, how long it takes, and whether any request is stuck without an issue.
dashboards.notes: Ported from observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json (Phase 6, AECI-219). The request→Linear pipeline: issue creation, the site→Linear resolution push, inbound webhooks, and the every-15-minute reconciliation sweep.

dashboards.name: AECi — Scheduled jobs and data cleanup
previousNames: AECi — Cron health & retention
dashboards.description: Thirteen jobs run on a schedule — hourly, nightly, one weekly. This board answers two questions: did each one run recently, and did any of them fail? It also carries the nightly data-quality findings and how much old data the cleanup job removed. Note that a job which stops running disappears from here rather than turning red; the check that can actually page you for an absent job runs outside PostHog.
dashboards.notes: NEW — no Datadog board equivalent; cron health lived only in monitors. Carries (a) the in-product mirror of the external liveness sweep, (b) the per-job failure roll-up, and (c) the two non-paging Datadog monitors the spec §5 table routes to 'digest': 'Retention prune skipped (metrics_daily gap)' and 'Data quality check found WARN-severity issues'. Both keep their old thresholds in observability/posthog/README.md.

dashboards.name: AECi — What the alerts are watching
previousNames: AECi — Alert signal sources
dashboards.description: One tile per alert email we are able to send, each showing the exact number that alert is judging right now. Read it top to bottom to see what every alert currently sees. It is a control panel, not a browsing surface — go to the topic boards for detail, and do not add breakdowns here (each tile has to return exactly one row or its alert has nothing to evaluate).
dashboards.notes: One insight per PostHog alert. Every alert must be attached to an insight, and every one of these returns EXACTLY ONE ROW by construction (an aggregate with no GROUP BY), so a healthy-but-empty window evaluates to 0 rather than to 'no rows' — which is the shape that makes a threshold alert safe. Reading this board top to bottom tells you what every alert currently sees. Do not add breakdowns here; use the topic boards for that.

insights.name: Page speed by type of page
previousNames: AECi — Traffic — SSR render volume and latency by route class
insights.dashboard: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
insights.description: How many pages we rendered and how long the average one took, split by the kind of page (home, product detail, listing) and whether it was cacheable. One page type being slow points at that page's data rather than at the site as a whole.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Top routes by request count (SSR route_class)' + 'Page render duration per route_class — p50/p95/p99'. p50/p99 are not reconstructed: the OTLP explicit-bucket histogram gives an exact bucket-upper-bound percentile, and one (p95, the one that carried a monitor) is enough here.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard.json widgets 1 + 3.
-- `count` is the OTLP histogram observation count, `value` the sum of observations,
-- so mean = sum(value)/sum(count). p95 is the upper bound of the bucket the 95th
-- observation falls in — see the 'AECi — ALERT' insight of the same shape for the
-- guard rails (overflow sentinel + minimum sample).
SELECT
    m.attributes.route_class                                          AS route_class,
    lower(m.attributes.cache_status)                                  AS cache_status,
    toInt(sum(m.count))                                               AS renders,
    round(sum(m.value) / greatest(sum(m.count), 1), 1)                AS mean_ms
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.page.render.duration_ms'
GROUP BY route_class, cache_status
ORDER BY renders DESC

insights.name: Page speed spread — how many were fast, how many were slow
previousNames: AECi — Traffic — SSR render latency distribution (histogram buckets)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
insights.description: The same renders as above, but counted into speed bands instead of averaged: how many came back under a tenth of a second, how many took over a second, and so on. An average hides a slow tail; this does not. When a percentile elsewhere looks wrong, trust this tile — it is a straight count with no arithmetic applied to it.
insights.notes: The exact latency shape, with no percentile reconstruction at all: observation counts per explicit OTLP bucket. This is the widget to trust while PostHog Metrics is still alpha — it is a straight read of what the transport sent.
insights.query:
-- Bucket bounds are pinned by the transport (spec §2):
--   [5,10,25,50,75,100,250,500,750,1000,1500,2500,5000,7500,10000] ms
-- `histogram_counts` has bounds.length + 1 entries; the last is the +Inf overflow bucket,
-- rendered below as the string '>10000'.
--
-- One ROW per bucket, two columns. The first version arrayJoin'd a zipped tuple into a
-- single column, so the tile rendered a stack of `('<=250', 41)` literals — correct data,
-- unreadable and un-sortable. Splitting the tuple costs nothing and makes it a table.
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT
        sumForEach(m.histogram_counts) AS counts,
        any(m.histogram_bounds)        AS bounds
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
      AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.page.render.duration_ms'
),
exploded AS (
    SELECT
        arrayJoin(
            arrayZip(
                arrayEnumerate(counts),
                arrayMap(i -> if(i > length(bounds), '>10000', concat('<=', toString(bounds[i]))),
                         arrayEnumerate(counts)),
                counts
            )
        ) AS row
    FROM agg
)
SELECT
    row.2                   AS bucket_ms,
    toInt(row.3)            AS renders
FROM exploded
ORDER BY row.1

insights.name: API endpoints — how busy and how slow
previousNames: AECi — Traffic — API query volume and p95 by endpoint
insights.dashboard: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
insights.description: Every API endpoint over the last day: how often it was called, plus the response time that 95% of its calls stayed below. Endpoints are grouped by their shape, so every product shares one row rather than getting one each.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'p95 API query duration per endpoint'. Tagged by MATCHED ROUTE PATTERN (e.g. /api/products/:slug), never the concrete path — the §3.5 cardinality rule. Note AECI-563: on /api/promote this now times only the fast kick-off; the ingest is aeci.api.promote.job.duration_ms.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard.json widget 4.
WITH per_endpoint AS (
    SELECT
        m.attributes.endpoint          AS endpoint,
        sumForEach(m.histogram_counts) AS counts,
        any(m.histogram_bounds)        AS bounds
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
      AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.api.query.duration_ms'
    GROUP BY endpoint
)
SELECT
    endpoint,
    toInt(arraySum(counts)) AS requests,
    arrayPushBack(bounds, 999999.0)[
        greatest(indexOf(arrayMap(c -> c >= 0.95 * arraySum(counts), arrayCumSum(counts)), 1), 1)
    ] AS p95_bucket_upper_ms
FROM per_endpoint
ORDER BY requests DESC
LIMIT 40

insights.name: Failed requests per hour
previousNames: AECi — Traffic — 4xx / 5xx rate per hour, both Workers
insights.dashboard: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
insights.description: The share of requests that came back as an error, hour by hour, across both the website and the API. Roughly: 4xx means a request was invalid, unauthorized, rate-limited or not found; 5xx means something failed on our server. The 5xx line is the number the error alert judges — this is the same thing with the shape left in, so you can tell a spike from a drift.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: '4xx / 5xx error rate over time (both Workers)'. Same numerator/denominator as the 'Worker error rate' alert, but broken out per hour so you can see the shape rather than the single number the alert evaluates.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard.json widget 5.
-- lower() on status_class is defensive, not cosmetic: Datadog lowercased tag values on
-- ingest and PostHog does not, so any casing assumption carried over from the Datadog
-- queries is a silent-zero waiting to happen. See README.md §'Migration hazards'.
SELECT
    toStartOfHour(m.timestamp)                                                   AS hour,
    toInt(sum(m.count))                                                          AS requests,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.count, lower(m.attributes.status_class) = '4xx')
          / greatest(sum(m.count), 1), 3)                                        AS rate_4xx_pct,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.count, lower(m.attributes.status_class) = '5xx')
          / greatest(sum(m.count), 1), 3)                                        AS rate_5xx_pct
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.page.render.duration_ms', 'aeci.api.query.duration_ms')
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Cache clears — what triggered them, and did they work
previousNames: AECi — Traffic — cache purges by source and outcome
insights.dashboard: AECi — Traffic, speed and errors
insights.description: Every time we wiped cached pages so a change would show up, what set it off (a catalogue update, a moderation decision, a manual purge) and whether it succeeded. Failed clears are worth chasing: they mean visitors carry on seeing the old page.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Cache purge events by source'. Extended with `outcome` because the WC-5/WC-6 split gave the consumer its own failure vocabulary (purge_failed / no_cache / noop) that the Datadog widget could not see.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard.json widget 6.
SELECT
    m.attributes.source  AS source,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    m.attributes.mode    AS mode,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS purges
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.cache.purge'
GROUP BY source, outcome, mode
ORDER BY purges DESC

insights.name: Catalogue to Algolia — did the sync run and did it work
previousNames: AECi — Search — Algolia sync runs by outcome, entity and trigger
insights.dashboard: AECi — Search
insights.description: Each run of the job that pushes our catalogue into Algolia over the last fortnight: what started it, what it was syncing, and whether it finished. A failure here means search results go stale, not that search stops working.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Algolia sync runs by outcome' + 'by entity and trigger', merged — HogQL returns all three dimensions in one table where Datadog needed two widgets.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json widgets 1 + 2.
SELECT
    m.attributes.trigger AS trigger,
    m.attributes.entity  AS entity,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS runs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.algolia.sync'
GROUP BY trigger, entity, outcome
ORDER BY runs DESC

insights.name: Sync speed and how many records moved
previousNames: AECi — Search — Algolia sync duration and records pushed
insights.dashboard: AECi — Search
insights.description: How long each Algolia sync took and how many records it added, updated or deleted. A sudden jump in the record count usually means a bulk catalogue change upstream, which is worth knowing about before someone reports search looking different.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Sync duration — p50/p95/p99 (by trigger)' + 'Records pushed per entity (saved/deleted)'. aeci.algolia.sync.records submits the RECORD COUNT as its value, not 1 — so it is summed, not counted.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json widgets 3 + 4.
SELECT 'duration'                                                    AS section,
       m.attributes.trigger                                          AS dimension_a,
       ''                                                            AS dimension_b,
       toInt(sum(m.count))                                           AS runs,
       round(sum(m.value) / greatest(sum(m.count), 1), 1)            AS mean_ms_or_records
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.algolia.sync.duration_ms'
GROUP BY dimension_a
UNION ALL
SELECT 'records'                                                     AS section,
       m.attributes.entity                                           AS dimension_a,
       m.attributes.op                                               AS dimension_b,
       0                                                             AS runs,
       sum(m.value)                                                  AS mean_ms_or_records
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.algolia.sync.records'
GROUP BY dimension_a, dimension_b
ORDER BY section, dimension_a, dimension_b

insights.name: Is Algolia out of step with our database?
previousNames: AECi — Search — Algolia index drift and orphan sweep per index
insights.dashboard: AECi — Search
insights.description: For each search index: how far the Algolia copy has drifted from our own database, and what the clean-up sweep removed. Anything other than zero drift means search can offer a result that no longer exists. Small drift normally repairs itself at the next morning sync, so a number here is a thing to watch rather than to act on.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Index drift per index (AECI-140)'. Also carries the REPORT-ONLY value half of the dual Datadog monitor 'AECi — Algolia index drift (D1 ≠ Algolia)' (threshold: abs(drift) > 0 over 1d) — spec §5 routes the value half here and the liveness half to the CI sweep.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json widget 5,
-- plus the AECI-266 orphan-sweep gauges the Datadog board never showed.
SELECT
    m.metric_name              AS metric,
    m.attributes.index         AS index_name,
    m.attributes.entity        AS entity,
    argMax(m.value, m.timestamp) AS latest_value,
    max(m.timestamp)           AS last_seen
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.algolia.index_drift',
      'aeci.algolia.orphans_removed',
      'aeci.algolia.orphans_skipped_cap')
GROUP BY metric, index_name, entity
ORDER BY metric, index_name

insights.name: How fast search feels to a visitor
previousNames: AECi — Search — browser query latency by result bucket (consented slice)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Search
insights.description: Search speed measured in the visitor's own browser, grouped by how many results came back — searches that find nothing behave differently from searches that find hundreds. Covers only visitors who accepted analytics cookies.
insights.notes: RE-HOMED (spec §3.9). Datadog source: 'Search query latency — p50/p95/p99 (browser RUM, AECI-174)'. Two accepted narrowings: the RUM action saw every search, this sees only the consented slice; and the action carried `index` while search_performed does not, so the per-index split is lost. Grouped by results_bucket instead. Full note in observability/posthog/README.md.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json widget 6.
-- Reads the PRODUCT-ANALYTICS event, not a metric — hence `events`, not posthog.metrics.
-- `status` / `duration_ms` / `results_bucket` are already on the searchPerformed()
-- signature (apps/web/src/app/analytics/analytics.ts); `index` is NOT, so the RUM
-- action's per-index split does not survive the re-home. Until prod carries these
-- properties the columns read null and this is empty rather than wrong — PostHog's
-- taxonomy warning on `duration_ms` is the expected pre-AW2 state.
SELECT
    properties.results_bucket                                                 AS results_bucket,
    count()                                                                   AS queries,
    round(avg(toFloatOrNull(toString(properties.duration_ms))), 1)            AS mean_ms,
    round(quantile(0.95)(toFloatOrNull(toString(properties.duration_ms))), 1) AS p95_ms
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND event = 'search_performed'
GROUP BY results_bucket
ORDER BY queries DESC

insights.name: Searches that failed outright, by day
previousNames: AECi — Search — browser query error rate (consented slice)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Search
insights.description: The share of searches that errored in the visitor's browser rather than returning results, day by day. Same consented-visitors-only caveat as the tile above.
insights.notes: RE-HOMED (spec §3.9). Datadog source: 'Search query error rate (%) (browser RUM, AECI-174)'. The Datadog widget had to restrict the denominator to @context.index:(products OR federated) because one successful /search query emitted TWO ok actions while a failure emitted ONE — the event carries one row per query, so that correction is no longer needed.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-search.json widget 7.
-- The Datadog widget had to restrict its denominator to @context.index:(products OR
-- federated) because ONE successful /search query emitted TWO ok RUM actions (one per
-- index) while a failure emitted ONE federated error — counting all actions halved the
-- apparent error rate. search_performed is one row per query, so that correction is
-- gone along with the `index` dimension that made it necessary.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(timestamp) AS day,
    count()                 AS queries,
    round(100.0 * countIf(toString(properties.status) = 'error') / greatest(count(), 1), 2) AS error_rate_pct
FROM events
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND event = 'search_performed'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 60

insights.name: Home-page number crunch — did it run and did it work
previousNames: AECi — Home stats — compute runs by outcome and duration
insights.dashboard: AECi — Home page numbers and page-view logging
insights.description: The job that recalculates the headline counts on the home page. Shows what triggered each run and whether it finished. When this fails the home page does not break — it just quietly keeps showing yesterday's figures.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Stats compute runs by outcome' + 'Stats compute duration — p50/p95/p99'.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-home-stats.json widgets 1 + 2.
SELECT
    m.attributes.trigger AS trigger,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS runs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.stats.compute'
GROUP BY trigger, outcome
ORDER BY runs DESC

insights.name: Which home-page figure failed
previousNames: AECi — Home stats — per-key outcome (which key failed)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Home page numbers and page-view logging
insights.description: The home-page calculation does one figure at a time, and one can fail without stopping the others. So a single wrong number on an otherwise healthy home page shows up here rather than in the run above.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Per-key compute outcome (which key failed)' + 'Per-key compute duration — p95 (by key)'. Per-key is best-effort: one key failing does not abort the rest, which is exactly why the per-key breakdown exists.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-home-stats.json widgets 3 + 4.
SELECT
    m.attributes.key     AS stats_cache_key,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS runs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.stats.compute.key'
GROUP BY stats_cache_key, outcome
ORDER BY stats_cache_key, outcome

insights.name: Page-view logging — successes, failures and bot traffic
previousNames: Page-view logging — successes, failures and how much is bots
AECi — Page views — writes by outcome and bot class
insights.dashboard: AECi — Home page numbers and page-view logging
insights.description: Every attempt to record a page view, by day, split by whether it worked and whether we judged the visitor to be automated. Roughly nine in ten page views in production are bots, so a high bot share is the normal state and not an incident.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Page-view writes by outcome'. Extended with the AECI-526 `bot` tag so the human/bot ratio is readable here rather than only in the daily digest — prod page_views has historically been ~89% bot.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-home-stats.json widget 5.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    m.attributes.outcome      AS outcome,
    m.attributes.bot          AS bot,
    toInt(sum(m.value))       AS writes
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.pageviews.write'
GROUP BY day, outcome, bot
ORDER BY day DESC, writes DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Page-view logging failure rate per hour
previousNames: AECi — Page views — write error rate per hour (%)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Home page numbers and page-view logging
insights.description: The share of page-view records that failed to save, hour by hour. While this is high, the traffic figures on the admin panel are undercounting real visits.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Page-view write error rate (%)'. Same numerator/denominator as the page_views alert, per hour.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-home-stats.json widget 6.
SELECT
    toStartOfHour(m.timestamp) AS hour,
    toInt(sum(m.value))        AS writes,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
          / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 2) AS error_rate_pct
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.pageviews.write'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Sign-ins — how people signed in, and whether it worked
previousNames: AECi — Auth — sign-ins by method and outcome
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: Completed sign-in attempts split by method (emailed link or Google) and outcome, with the reason attached to failures. Counts completions only: someone who asks for a link and never clicks it does not appear here at all.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Sign-ins by outcome' + 'Sign-ins by method', merged. Emitted from the SSR Worker at /auth/callback, so these rows carry service=aeci-web, NOT aeci-api. 'Attempts' = the sum over outcomes (one per sign-in COMPLETION); browser-side initiation is not counted.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widgets 1 + 2.
SELECT
    m.attributes.method  AS method,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    m.attributes.reason  AS failure_reason,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS signins
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.auth.signin'
GROUP BY method, outcome, failure_reason
ORDER BY signins DESC

insights.name: Sign-in failure rate per hour
previousNames: AECi — Auth — sign-in failure rate per hour (%)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: The share of sign-in attempts that failed, hour by hour. This is the number behind the sign-in alert. Read the attempt count next to it — at our volume one failure in a quiet hour looks far more dramatic than it is.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Auth failure rate (%)'. Per hour, so the alert's single hourly number can be read in context.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widget 3.
SELECT
    toStartOfHour(m.timestamp) AS hour,
    toInt(sum(m.value))        AS attempts,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
          / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1) AS failure_rate_pct
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.auth.signin'
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Reviews submitted, by day
previousNames: AECi — Reviews — submits by outcome
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: How many reviews people submitted each day, and whether each one was accepted, turned away as a duplicate, or aimed at a product we do not list.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Review submits by outcome'. outcome ∈ ok / duplicate / product_not_found.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widget 4.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    m.attributes.outcome      AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))       AS submits
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.review.submit'
GROUP BY day, outcome
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: What moderators did
previousNames: AECi — Moderation — actions, bans and request moderation
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: Moderation activity over the last month: actions taken on reviews, users banned, and decisions made on vendor requests — with whether an admin or a moderator did it.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Moderation actions by action / outcome'. Extended with aeci.moderation.ban (AECI-218/524, with the AECI-524 role tag) and aeci.request.moderation.action (AECI-216) — both shipped after the Datadog board was exported and were never added to it.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widget 5.
SELECT
    m.metric_name        AS metric,
    m.attributes.action  AS action,
    m.attributes.role    AS role,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS actions
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.moderation.action',
      'aeci.moderation.ban',
      'aeci.request.moderation.action')
GROUP BY metric, action, role, outcome
ORDER BY metric, actions DESC

insights.name: Automatic abuse screening — volume, failures and why
previousNames: AECi — Toxicity — scoring volume, error rate and latency
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: Every review is scored for abusive language so the moderation queue can float the worst content to the top. Shows how many were scored each day, how many scoring calls failed, and why. Scoring never blocks a review — when it fails the review is still saved, it just arrives in the queue without a priority score.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Toxicity scoring latency — p50/p95/p99' + 'Toxicity scoring error rate (%)', merged. Backed by Claude Haiku since AECI-258 (Perspective API sunset).
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widgets 6 + 7.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    toInt(sum(m.value))       AS calls,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
          / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1) AS error_rate_pct,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(toString(m.attributes.reason),
                                       m.attributes.outcome = 'failed'), ', ') AS failure_reasons
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.toxicity.api'
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 100

insights.name: Moderation queue — how deep, and how long the oldest has waited
previousNames: AECi — Moderation — queue depth and oldest pending age
insights.dashboard: AECi — Sign-ins, reviews and moderation
insights.description: A once-a-day snapshot: how many items are waiting for a moderator, and how long the oldest one has been sitting there. An oldest item past about two days means the queue is not being worked, whatever the depth says.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Moderation queue — oldest pending age (h) + depth'. Also carries the BACKLOG half of the dual Datadog monitor 'AECi — Moderation queue backlog (oldest pending > 48h)' — spec §5 routes the backlog half to dashboard/digest and the liveness half to the CI sweep. Old threshold: oldest pending > 48h over 1d.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-auth-reviews.json widget 8.
-- Gauges: read the LATEST sample per day, not a sum. The 06:00 UTC cron writes one
-- sample per day, so argMax collapses to that sample.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    argMaxIf(m.value, m.timestamp, m.metric_name = 'aeci.moderation.queue_depth')             AS queue_depth,
    argMaxIf(m.value, m.timestamp, m.metric_name = 'aeci.moderation.queue_oldest_age_hours')  AS oldest_pending_hours
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 60 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.moderation.queue_depth', 'aeci.moderation.queue_oldest_age_hours')
GROUP BY day
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 100

insights.name: Linear issues opened from site requests
previousNames: AECi — Linear — issue creation by outcome and kind
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: Claims and corrections submitted on the site become Linear issues. Shows how many were created, of which kind, and why any failed. 'Skipped' means the issue already existed — that is the system safely handling a repeat, not an error.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Linear issue creation by outcome' + 'by kind', merged. outcome ∈ ok / failed / skipped_exists (an idempotent re-fire); kind ∈ claim / correction.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widgets 1 + 2.
SELECT
    m.attributes.kind    AS kind,
    m.attributes.outcome AS outcome,
    m.attributes.reason  AS failure_reason,
    toInt(sum(m.value))  AS issues
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.issue'
GROUP BY kind, outcome, failure_reason
ORDER BY issues DESC

insights.name: Request-to-Linear failure rate per hour
previousNames: AECi — Linear — pipeline failure rate per hour (%)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: The share of hand-offs to Linear that failed outright. Safe repeats are left out of the sum on purpose: counting them would let a burst of resubmissions disguise a real outage as a healthy-looking percentage.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Linear issue creation failure rate (%)' + 'Site→Linear sync' failure rate. Same numerator/denominator as the pipeline alert. The skipped_* outcomes are excluded from the denominator: an idempotent re-fire or a no-issue sync is not a terminal attempt.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widget 3.
SELECT
    toStartOfHour(m.timestamp) AS hour,
    toInt(sum(m.value))        AS terminal_attempts,
    round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
          / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1) AS failure_rate_pct
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.linear.issue', 'aeci.linear.sync')
  AND m.attributes.outcome NOT IN ('skipped_exists', 'skipped_no_issue')
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Pushing decisions back to the site
previousNames: AECi — Linear — site→Linear sync by outcome and target status
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: When an issue is resolved or rejected in Linear we push that decision back to the site so the requester sees it. Shows how many pushes happened, to which status, and whether they landed.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Site→Linear sync by outcome' + 'by target status', merged. to_status ∈ resolved / rejected.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widgets 5 + 6.
SELECT
    m.attributes.to_status AS to_status,
    m.attributes.kind      AS kind,
    m.attributes.outcome   AS outcome,
    toInt(sum(m.value))    AS syncs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.sync'
GROUP BY to_status, kind, outcome
ORDER BY syncs DESC

insights.name: How slow the Linear hand-off is
previousNames: AECi — Linear — issue and sync latency
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: The response time that 95% of calls stayed below, for both directions of the Linear hand-off. Linear is somebody else's API, so this mostly measures them — it is here to tell you whether a slow request queue is our fault or theirs.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Linear issue creation latency — p50/p95/p99' + 'Site→Linear sync latency — p50/p95/p99'.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widgets 4 + 7.
WITH per_metric AS (
    SELECT
        m.metric_name                  AS metric,
        sumForEach(m.histogram_counts) AS counts,
        any(m.histogram_bounds)        AS bounds
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
      AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.linear.issue.duration_ms', 'aeci.linear.sync.duration_ms')
    GROUP BY metric
)
SELECT
    metric,
    toInt(arraySum(counts)) AS calls,
    arrayPushBack(bounds, 999999.0)[
        greatest(indexOf(arrayMap(c -> c >= 0.95 * arraySum(counts), arrayCumSum(counts)), 1), 1)
    ] AS p95_bucket_upper_ms
FROM per_metric
ORDER BY metric

insights.name: Messages coming in from Linear — and ones we refused
previousNames: AECi — Linear — inbound webhook receipts and HMAC failures
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: Linear tells us when an issue changes. Shows what we received, and separately how many messages we threw away because the signature did not check out. A run of refusals means either the shared secret was changed without telling us, or someone is poking at the endpoint.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Linear webhook receipts by action' + 'Linear webhook HMAC failures'. HMAC failures also carry an alert (>3/1h) — this is the shape behind that number.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widgets 8 + 9.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    m.metric_name             AS metric,
    m.attributes.type         AS resource_type,
    m.attributes.action       AS action,
    toInt(sum(m.value))       AS events
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.webhooks.linear.receipt', 'aeci.webhooks.linear.hmac_failure')
GROUP BY day, metric, resource_type, action
ORDER BY day DESC, events DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Stuck requests and the retry sweep
previousNames: AECi — Linear — reconciliation backlog, attempts and alert emails
insights.dashboard: AECi — Vendor requests and their Linear issues
insights.description: A sweep runs every fifteen minutes looking for site requests whose Linear issue never got created, retries them, and emails an admin when one keeps failing. Shows the backlog, the retries, and the failures that stopped being retryable. A number in that last column is a real person's request sitting unanswered.
insights.notes: Datadog parity: 'Reconciliation backlog — stuck rows (gauge)' + 'Reconciliation attempts by outcome' + 'Reconciliation persistent failures' + 'Admin-alert email seam by outcome'. reconcile.attempt / .persistent_failure submit the ROW COUNT as their value, so they are summed; .stuck is a gauge read with argMax.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/dashboard-requests-moderation.json widgets 10–13.
SELECT
    toStartOfHour(m.timestamp) AS hour,
    argMaxIf(m.value, m.timestamp, m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.reconcile.stuck')   AS backlog_stuck_rows,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.reconcile.attempt'))          AS retry_attempts,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.reconcile.persistent_failure')) AS persistent_failures,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.reconcile.email'))            AS admin_alert_emails
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.linear.reconcile.stuck',
      'aeci.linear.reconcile.attempt',
      'aeci.linear.reconcile.persistent_failure',
      'aeci.linear.reconcile.email')
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Did every scheduled job run? (last sign of life)
previousNames: AECi — Crons — last heartbeat per job (in-product mirror of the CI sweep)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Scheduled jobs and data cleanup
insights.description: Each scheduled job's most recent sign of life and how long ago it was. Read the limitation before you trust it: a job that stops entirely vanishes from this list rather than turning red, and a check living inside the system cannot notice its own death — so the alarm for an absent job is a separate check that runs on GitHub Actions every three hours. This tile is the convenient view, not the safety net.
insights.notes: NEW. The in-product mirror of scripts/ci/posthog-liveness-sweep.sh. It is a MIRROR, not the mechanism: an insight cannot page on absence, and a check that lives inside the system it watches cannot detect its own death — which is exactly why the sweep runs on GitHub Actions instead. If a job is missing from this table entirely, that IS the absence.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Same thirteen heartbeat series as observability/posthog/project-config.json
-- `liveness.crons[].metric`. Keep the two lists in step.
-- The window is 15 DAY, not 72 HOUR: `aeci.asn_registry.refresh` is WEEKLY (AECI-750), so a
-- 72 h window would report it missing six days out of seven. Matches liveness.lookbackHours=360.
SELECT
    m.metric_name                                        AS heartbeat_metric,
    max(m.timestamp)                                     AS last_seen,
    dateDiff('minute', max(m.timestamp), now())          AS age_minutes,
    toInt(count())                                       AS points_in_window
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 15 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.metrics_snapshot.run',
      'aeci.asn_registry.refresh',
      'aeci.retention.prune',
      'aeci.data_quality.job',
      'aeci.analytics_digest.email',
      'aeci.moderation.queue_depth',
      'aeci.stats.compute',
      'aeci.algolia.sync',
      'aeci.algolia.index_drift',
      'aeci.attestation.notify.job',
      'aeci.entitlement.expiry.job',
      'aeci.linear.reconcile.stuck',
      'aeci.waf.poll')
GROUP BY heartbeat_metric
ORDER BY age_minutes DESC

insights.name: Scheduled jobs that failed, last 7 days
previousNames: AECi — Crons — failed runs by job (last 7 days)
insights.dashboard: AECi — Scheduled jobs and data cleanup
insights.description: Which job failed, on which day, and what had triggered the run. One alert covers all thirteen jobs, so this is where you come after a 'scheduled job failed' email to find out which one it was.
insights.notes: NEW. The breakdown behind the combined 'Cron job failed (any job)' alert: which job, on which day. Four Datadog monitors (Algolia sync / home stats / data quality / retention prune failed) collapsed into that one alert; this is where you find out which of them fired.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Ports the four Datadog *-failed monitors as a breakdown.
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    m.metric_name             AS job_metric,
    m.attributes.trigger      AS trigger,
    toInt(sum(m.value))       AS failed_runs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 7 DAY
  AND m.attributes.outcome = 'failed'
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.metrics_snapshot.run',
      'aeci.asn_registry.refresh',
      'aeci.retention.prune',
      'aeci.data_quality.job',
      'aeci.analytics_digest.email',
      'aeci.stats.compute',
      'aeci.stats.compute.key',
      'aeci.algolia.sync',
      'aeci.attestation.notify.job',
      'aeci.entitlement.expiry.job',
      'aeci.waf.poll')
GROUP BY day, job_metric, trigger
ORDER BY day DESC, failed_runs DESC

insights.name: Nightly data-quality checks
previousNames: AECi — Data quality — findings by check and severity
insights.dashboard: AECi — Scheduled jobs and data cleanup
insights.description: A nightly sweep looks for data that does not add up — records pointing at things that no longer exist, counts that disagree with each other. Each row is one check on one day and how many problems it found. A check that crashed says 'CHECK THREW' rather than reporting a clean zero, which is the distinction worth watching for.
insights.notes: Carries the Datadog monitor 'AECi — Data quality check found WARN-severity issues (by check)', which spec §5 routes to the digest (non-paging). Old threshold: max value by check > 0 over 1d, severity:warn. The ERROR-severity half keeps a real alert. A check that THREW emits the sentinel -1.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Source: observability/datadog/monitor-data-quality-check-warn.json
-- (digest/report-only) + monitor-data-quality-check.json (alerted separately).
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp)    AS day,
    m.attributes.check           AS check_id,
    m.attributes.severity        AS severity,
    argMax(m.value, m.timestamp) AS findings,
    if(argMax(m.value, m.timestamp) < 0, 'CHECK THREW', '') AS note
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 14 DAY
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.data_quality.check'
GROUP BY day, check_id, severity
ORDER BY day DESC, severity, findings DESC
LIMIT 300

insights.name: Old-data cleanup — what was deleted, and what was not
previousNames: AECi — Retention — rows deleted, skipped and truncated runs
insights.dashboard: AECi — Scheduled jobs and data cleanup
insights.description: How much old data the nightly cleanup removed from each table. The column to watch is the skipped one: when the job cannot confirm a day's traffic was already summed up, it refuses to delete anything at all that day, so old data quietly piles up while every run still reports success.
insights.notes: Carries the Datadog monitor 'AECi — Retention prune skipped (metrics_daily gap)', which spec §5 routes to the digest (non-paging). Old threshold: sum of outcome:skipped > 0 over 1d. `skipped` is the one to watch: a day inside the page_views cut window with no metrics_daily row makes the prune refuse to delete from EITHER table. The runaway threshold (>5,000 rows/table/day) keeps a real alert.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Sources: monitor-retention-prune-skipped.json (digest) +
-- monitor-retention-prune-runaway.json (alerted separately).
SELECT
    toStartOfDay(m.timestamp) AS day,
    m.attributes.table        AS target_table,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.retention.rows_deleted'))       AS rows_deleted,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.retention.prune.truncated'))    AS truncated_runs,
    toInt(sumIf(m.value, m.metric_name = 'aeci.retention.prune'
                         AND m.attributes.outcome = 'skipped'))                AS skipped_runs,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(toString(m.attributes.reason),
                                       m.attributes.outcome = 'skipped'), ', ') AS skip_reason
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.retention.rows_deleted',
      'aeci.retention.prune',
      'aeci.retention.prune.truncated')
GROUP BY day, target_table
ORDER BY day DESC
LIMIT 200

insights.name: Alert: server errors above 1%
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Worker 5xx rate (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Sends an email when more than one request in a hundred came back as a server error over the last hour, across the website and the API together. A very quiet hour reads zero rather than reacting to a single bad request out of a handful.
insights.notes: Fires when 5xx responses exceed 1% of Worker-run requests across BOTH Workers in the last hour. Datadog evaluated the same ratio every 5 minutes; hourly is the PostHog floor (spec D3) and is the single largest cadence loss in this migration.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-error-rate.json.
-- Denominator floor of 50: at low traffic a single 5xx is >1% and would page on noise.
-- Datadog's 5-minute window had the same exposure; the floor is new and deliberate.
-- `count` is the OTLP histogram observation count — the exact analogue of Datadog's
-- count:<distribution>. Note (§8.2) raw status_code was dropped from the render metric
-- for cardinality; status_class survives and is what this reads.
SELECT
    if(sum(m.count) >= 50,
       round(100.0 * sumIf(m.count, lower(m.attributes.status_class) = '5xx')
             / greatest(sum(m.count), 1), 3),
       0.0)                                                        AS error_rate_pct,
    concat(toString(toInt(sum(m.count))), ' Worker-run requests in 1h; ',
           toString(toInt(sumIf(m.count, lower(m.attributes.status_class) = '5xx'))),
           ' were 5xx')                                            AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.page.render.duration_ms', 'aeci.api.query.duration_ms')

insights.name: Alert: a scheduled job failed
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Cron job failed (any of the thirteen, 24 h)
AECi — ALERT — Cron job failed (any of the twelve, 24 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: One alert covering all thirteen scheduled jobs. The email names the job or jobs that failed, so bundling them together loses nothing. Anything above zero means at least one run failed during the last 24 hours.
insights.notes: COMBINED. One alert covering every scheduled job's failure heartbeat; the breach message names which job(s) via label_column, so combining costs nothing an operator would have used. Replaces four separate Datadog monitors and adds coverage for six crons Datadog never watched.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces FOUR Datadog monitors:
--   monitor-algolia-sync-failed.json, monitor-stats-compute-failed.json,
--   monitor-data-quality-failed.json, monitor-retention-prune-failed.json
-- and ADDS the six crons Datadog had no failure monitor for: metrics-snapshot,
-- analytics-digest, attestation-notify, entitlement-expiry, waf-poll, and the
-- per-key half of home-stats.
--
-- No `trigger:cron` predicate, deliberately: aeci.algolia.sync and aeci.stats.compute
-- also fire on trigger:promote, and a promote-path failure is a real failure. Datadog's
-- Algolia monitor was already trigger-agnostic; its stats monitor was not, and that gap
-- is closed here.
--
-- The aggregate has no GROUP BY, so it ALWAYS returns exactly one row (0 / '') even on
-- a totally empty window. That is the shape a threshold alert needs — a query that can
-- return zero rows has nothing for the alert to evaluate.
SELECT
    sum(m.value)                                                   AS failed_runs,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(m.metric_name), ', ')         AS failing_jobs
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
  AND m.attributes.outcome = 'failed'
  AND m.metric_name IN (
      'aeci.metrics_snapshot.run',
      'aeci.asn_registry.refresh',
      'aeci.retention.prune',
      'aeci.data_quality.job',
      'aeci.analytics_digest.email',
      'aeci.stats.compute',
      'aeci.stats.compute.key',
      'aeci.algolia.sync',
      'aeci.attestation.notify.job',
      'aeci.entitlement.expiry.job',
      'aeci.waf.poll')

insights.name: Alert: a data-quality check found something serious
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Data quality ERROR-severity findings (24 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: The nightly checks ran perfectly well and found something wrong in the data itself. A different problem from a failed job, and a different fix: nothing needs restarting, the data needs correcting. It also fires when a check crashes, so a broken check cannot pass itself off as a clean one.
insights.notes: Fires when any error-severity data-quality check reports a non-zero finding count OR throws. Distinct from the cron-failure alert: the job succeeded, the DATA is wrong. Different runbook, so it keeps its own alert.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-data-quality-check.json.
-- abs(), not max(): a check that THREW emits the sentinel -1, and Datadog's
-- `max:... by {check} > 0` could not see that — a thrown error-severity check was
-- silently indistinguishable from a clean one. Taking abs() closes that hole.
SELECT
    max(abs(m.value))                                                              AS worst_finding,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(toString(m.attributes.check), m.value != 0), ', ') AS failing_checks
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.data_quality.check'
  AND m.attributes.severity = 'error'

insights.name: Alert: the cleanup job deleted far more than expected
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Retention prune deleted an unexpected number of rows (24 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: A safety net on the one job that deletes data for good. It fires on a run that succeeded but did something suspicious — far more rows removed from a table than on a normal day — so you can inspect what was deleted while recovery is still possible.
insights.notes: The destructive-job safety valve. Kept as its own alert rather than folded into the combined cron-failure alert: a runaway prune is a SUCCESSFUL run with the wrong effect, and its runbook is 'check what was deleted before it ages out', not 'restart the job'.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-retention-prune-runaway.json.
-- aeci.retention.rows_deleted is emitted every run for every table, zeros included,
-- which is what makes a threshold (rather than a presence) test possible at all.
SELECT
    max(rows_deleted)                                                           AS max_rows_deleted,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(tbl, rows_deleted > 5000), ', ')         AS tables_over_budget
FROM (
    SELECT
        toString(m.attributes.table) AS tbl,
        sum(m.value)                 AS rows_deleted
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
      AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.retention.rows_deleted'
    GROUP BY tbl
)

insights.name: Alert: someone's request is stuck
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Linear reconciliation persistent failures (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: A claim or correction whose Linear issue has failed to be created several times. The retry sweep itself is still running, but a person's request is going unanswered. Open that request to diagnose and resolve the failure.
insights.notes: A user-visible vendor request whose Linear issue creation has failed repeatedly. Kept separate from the combined cron alert: the sweep itself is healthy, a REQUEST is stuck, and the operator action is to look at that request.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-linear-reconcile-stuck.json.
-- The metric submits the ROW COUNT as its value, not 1 — so it is summed, not counted.
SELECT
    sum(m.value)                                          AS persistent_failures,
    'vendor_requests stuck open with linear_issue_id=null after a retry' AS detail
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.linear.reconcile.persistent_failure'

insights.name: Alert: the search clean-up refused a large delete
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Algolia orphan sweep hit its safety cap (24 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: The sweep that removes stale search records has a ceiling, and it stopped rather than deleting a suspiciously large batch. The job succeeded; it simply declined to act, so someone needs to confirm the delete was really wanted.
insights.notes: The delete-only orphan sweep refused a large purge. Kept separate from the combined cron alert because the JOB SUCCEEDED — folding a success-with-a-caveat into 'job failed' would make that alert's meaning mushy.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-algolia-orphan-sweep-capped.json.
-- Emitted only when the cap actually refuses a purge, so a healthy window has no rows —
-- which is why this reads through a subquery aggregate that still yields one row.
SELECT
    max(skipped)                                                        AS max_skipped,
    arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(idx, skipped > 0), ', ')         AS capped_indexes
FROM (
    SELECT
        toString(m.attributes.index) AS idx,
        max(m.value)                 AS skipped
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR
      AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.algolia.orphans_skipped_cap'
    GROUP BY idx
)

insights.name: Alert: too many sign-ins are failing
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Auth sign-in failure rate (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Fires when more than 30% of sign-in attempts failed over the last hour. It evaluates only hours with at least five attempts, so a single failure during a quiet hour does not look like a crisis.
insights.notes: Datadog evaluated this over 15 minutes; hourly is the PostHog floor. Threshold unchanged at 30%. A minimum-denominator floor of 5 attempts is NEW — at AECi's sign-in volume a 1-of-2 failure is 50% and would have paged.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-auth-error-rate.json.
-- Emitted from the SSR Worker at /auth/callback, so these points carry service=aeci-web.
SELECT
    if(sum(m.value) >= 5,
       round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
             / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1),
       0.0)                                                          AS failure_rate_pct,
    concat(toString(toInt(sum(m.value))), ' sign-in completions in 1h') AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.auth.signin'

insights.name: Alert: abuse screening is failing
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Toxicity scoring failure rate (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Fires when more than half the abuse-screening calls failed over the last hour — usually the model provider having a bad day rather than anything wrong here. Reviews are still accepted while it fires; they just reach the moderation queue without a priority score.
insights.notes: Datadog evaluated over 15 minutes; hourly is the PostHog floor. Threshold unchanged at 50%. Minimum-denominator floor of 5 is new.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-toxicity-outage.json.
-- Backed by Claude Haiku since AECI-258 (Perspective API sunset) —
-- apps/api/src/lib/toxicity.ts.
SELECT
    if(sum(m.value) >= 5,
       round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
             / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1),
       0.0)                                                        AS failure_rate_pct,
    concat(toString(toInt(sum(m.value))), ' scoring calls in 1h; reasons: ',
           arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArrayIf(toString(m.attributes.reason),
                                              m.attributes.outcome = 'failed'), '/')) AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.toxicity.api'

insights.name: Alert: page-view logging is failing
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — page_views write failure rate (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Fires when more than one page view in ten failed to be recorded over the last hour. While it is firing, the traffic figures on the admin panel are undercounting.
insights.notes: Datadog evaluated over 10 minutes; hourly is the PostHog floor. Threshold unchanged at 10%. Minimum-denominator floor of 20 is new — page_views is the highest-volume write in the system, so 20/hour is a low bar that still suppresses the 3-request-hour false positive.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-pageviews-write-errors.json.
-- ADR 0022: page_views is a derived/log-class write and is exempt from audit_log — this
-- metric plus job_runs IS its observability.
SELECT
    if(sum(m.value) >= 20,
       round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
             / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 2),
       0.0)                                                        AS error_rate_pct,
    concat(toString(toInt(sum(m.value))), ' page-view writes in 1h') AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.pageviews.write'

insights.name: Alert: the Linear hand-off is failing
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Linear pipeline failure rate (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Fires when more than half of the genuine attempts to create or update a Linear issue failed over the last hour. Safe repeats are excluded from the sum so that they cannot dilute a real outage into a healthy-looking number.
insights.notes: Window unchanged at 1 h (Datadog already used last_1h); only the evaluation cadence moves to hourly. Threshold unchanged at 50%. Minimum-denominator floor of 3 is new.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-linear-pipeline-failure.json.
-- The skipped_* outcomes are excluded from the denominator, exactly as Datadog did:
-- an idempotent re-fire (skipped_exists) or a no-issue sync (skipped_no_issue) is not a
-- terminal attempt and counting it would dilute a real outage into invisibility.
SELECT
    if(sum(m.value) >= 3,
       round(100.0 * sumIf(m.value, m.attributes.outcome = 'failed')
             / greatest(sum(m.value), 1), 1),
       0.0)                                                        AS failure_rate_pct,
    concat(toString(toInt(sum(m.value))), ' terminal pipeline attempts in 1h') AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name IN ('aeci.linear.issue', 'aeci.linear.sync')
  AND m.attributes.outcome NOT IN ('skipped_exists', 'skipped_no_issue')

insights.name: Alert: we are refusing messages from Linear
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Linear webhook HMAC failures (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: We threw away more than three incoming Linear messages in an hour because the signature did not verify. Either the shared secret was changed on one side only, or somebody is probing the endpoint. Worth looking at promptly either way.
insights.notes: Security signal, unchanged in every respect: same 1 h window, same threshold of 3, only the evaluation cadence moves to hourly.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-webhook-hmac-failure.json.
-- Emitted BEFORE the 401 when Linear-Signature is missing or invalid. A sustained
-- non-zero series is either a rotated webhook secret or someone probing the endpoint.
SELECT
    sum(m.value)                                              AS hmac_failures,
    'POST /api/webhooks/linear rejected before handling'      AS detail
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.webhooks.linear.hmac_failure'

insights.name: Alert: an unusual burst of blocked traffic
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — WAF rate-limit / challenge volume (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Cloudflare's rate limits blocked far more requests than usual over the last hour — a scraper, a wave of bots, or an attack. The email names the rules that fired most, which is normally enough to tell which of the three it is.
insights.notes: THRESHOLD RESCALED, deliberately: Datadog fired on >500 blocked events in 15 minutes; the equivalent hourly rate is 500 x 4 = 2,000. The underlying data is unchanged — the source is an HOURLY cron reading the previous clock hour from Cloudflare's GraphQL API, so Datadog's 15-minute window was always coarser than it looked.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-waf-ratelimit-spike.json.
-- aeci.waf.ratelimit.blocked submits the EVENT COUNT as its value, not 1 — summed.
-- Scoped to this env's own host by the poll itself, so a shared zone is not counted
-- under every env tag.
SELECT
    sum(m.value)                                                                     AS blocked_events,
    concat('top rules: ',
           arrayStringConcat(arraySlice(arraySort(groupUniqArray(toString(m.attributes.rule))), 1, 5), ', ')) AS sample
FROM posthog.metrics AS m
WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
  AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.waf.ratelimit.blocked'

insights.name: Alert: product pages are rendering slowly
previousNames: AECi — ALERT — Detail page render p95, cache MISS (1 h)
insights.dashboard: AECi — What the alerts are watching
insights.description: Estimates the 95th-percentile product-page render time over the last hour — the time within which 95% of pages finished rendering — and fires when it exceeds a second and a half. It counts only pages our server actually built — a page served from the edge cache never reaches us — so the sample can be thin, and the alert deliberately stays quiet below twenty renders. The figure is a slight over-estimate by construction, which is the safe direction for an alert to lean.
insights.notes: PORTED with a caveat — read the query comments. PostHog stores our distributions as OTLP explicit-bucket histograms, so there is no percentile function: this p95 is the UPPER BOUND of the bucket the 95th observation falls in. Conservative by at most one bucket width (the right direction for an alert) but UNVERIFIED UNTIL DATA FLOWS — README.md manual step 2.
insights.query:
-- AECI-647 / PH-6. Replaces observability/datadog/monitor-detail-render-p95.json.
--
-- Bucket bounds are pinned by the transport (spec §2):
--   [5,10,25,50,75,100,250,500,750,1000,1500,2500,5000,7500,10000] ms
-- and histogram_counts carries bounds.length + 1 entries — the extra one is the +Inf
-- overflow bucket. `arrayPushBack(bounds, 999999.0)` gives that overflow bucket an edge:
-- without it a p95 above 10 s indexes past the end of `bounds`, ClickHouse returns the
-- 0 default, and the WORST case would silently fail to fire.
--
-- sumForEach() sums the count arrays element-wise across every data point. It is only
-- correct because every point shares one bound array; if a future metric ships different
-- bounds under the same name the arrays misalign silently. Do not reuse this shape
-- without re-checking that.
--
-- lower(cache_status): the SSR Worker emits the literal 'MISS' (server-runtime.ts:989).
-- Datadog lowercased tag values on ingest and PostHog does not, so a copied
-- `cache_status:miss` predicate would match nothing. See README.md §'Migration hazards'.
--
-- Under WC-8 a cache HIT skips the Worker entirely, so this series is MISS-only volume
-- and can be sparse. The 20-observation floor keeps a quiet hour from producing a p95
-- out of three samples.
WITH agg AS (
    SELECT
        sumForEach(m.histogram_counts) AS counts,
        any(m.histogram_bounds)        AS bounds
    FROM posthog.metrics AS m
    WHERE m.timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR
      AND m.metric_name = 'aeci.page.render.duration_ms'
      AND m.attributes.route_class = 'detail'
      AND lower(m.attributes.cache_status) = 'miss'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        arraySum(counts)                AS observations,
        arrayPushBack(bounds, 999999.0) AS edges,
        indexOf(arrayMap(c -> c >= 0.95 * arraySum(counts), arrayCumSum(counts)), 1) AS bucket_index
    FROM agg
)
SELECT
    if(observations < 20 OR bucket_index = 0, 0.0, edges[bucket_index]) AS p95_bucket_upper_ms,
    concat(toString(toInt(observations)), ' MISS detail renders in 1h') AS sample
FROM ranked
